title: Dribble Hand-Off Timing
description: Pairs practise the dribble hand-off: the dribbler hands the ball to a teammate cutting off their hip, then becomes a screen or rolls to the rim.

content.objective: Execute a safe, well-timed hand-off with a shielding body, and read the defense to shoot, drive or hit the roll.
content.setup: Dribbler at the top of the key, receiver at the wing.
instructions: The dribbler dribbles toward the wing receiver.
The receiver waits, then cuts tight off the dribbler's hip.
The dribbler stops, hands the ball with two hands, body sideways to protect it.
The receiver reads: shoot behind the hand-off, or drive if the defender trails.
The hand-off player rolls to the rim for a possible pass.
coachingPoints: Hand the ball, do not toss it.
The receiver cuts shoulder to hip, tight.
Set your feet at the hand-off: it is a screen.
commonMistakes: Receiver cutting too early and too wide.
Exposing the ball to the defender during the hand-off.
content.safety: 2v2 defenders fight over or under, not through, the screener.
regressions: Stationary hand-off without dribbling into it.
variations: Fake the hand-off and keep the ball (keeper).
successCriteria: Hand-off made with the ball shielded every time.
Receiver makes the correct read in 7 of 10 reps.
content.gameApplication: Hand-offs are a simple, safe way to start two-player actions, especially against pressure.
